text: In the twenty-second chapter of Genesis a question is raised and left without an answer. Abraham is commanded to take his son, his only son Isaac, whom he loves; and of what he feels at the command we are told nothing, for the narrator never describes what passes within him. He does not protest, nor does he bargain; of the man who once pleaded for Sodom nothing appears here. Abraham stands before us less as a character than as a silence, and that silence is the chief matter of the chapter.
